params.body:
## What

Maarten wants to offer the layers under Gentells to enterprise clients. In the conversation that started that, "graph", "taxonomy" and "ontology" were used for the same thing, and each promises a customer something different. This note says which of them we actually hold, measured on the box on 22 September, and what may be promised about each.

It sits beside the architecture paper rather than replacing it: the paper describes the system, this is the commercial inventory.

## What it says

**We hold vocabularies, a schema and a graph. We hold neither a taxonomy nor an ontology.** Nothing in `taxonomy.mjs` is nested (no parent, child, broader or narrower anywhere), and the rules that make a fact follow live in code, so a customer's instance cannot read them and cannot be checked against them.

**The graph is the weakest layer, and it is the one that sounds most sellable.** 64,776 of 66,263 edges carry exactly one weight, 1.0, because a model asserted them once and nothing tested them. Only `co-occurs` is measured (1,487 edges, 122 distinct weights), and it grew from 128 on 13 September, so the right layer is growing.

**This corrects the paper's thesis.** The paper says "the graph is the asset, and product surfaces are framed views into it". Measured, the memory is the asset: the corpus, the vocabulary over it, and the ladder that reads it. The edge layer is the weakest part of that memory, not its centre. The framed-views half stands.

**Two graphs, one method.** The shape worth selling is not access to ours but that a customer builds their own on our method, grounded by matching against our vocabulary. `tenant-boundary.mjs` already enforces the boundary in CI; what exists is the thin version (context into a prompt), and the structural version makes that test harder rather than easier. On-premise breaks the grounded form, so it splits three ways: publish the method, license a versioned copy of the vocabulary, or hand over the corpus, and only the first two are defensible.

**What may be promised per layer**, as a table, so a sales conversation has a floor.

**Four things it asks for next**, not scheduled: nesting in the closed lists, the rulebook as data (the move Elixir already made with its thresholds registry), thresholds that suit a small graph, and edges that earn their weight.

## Numbers in it

All from the live database on 22 September, or from the file named. 206,753 signals over 156 unbroken days; 76,337 concepts (1,500 confirmed); 66,263 edges; 7,247 signals (3.5%) ever cited; 1,232 of 10,176 patterns used; evidence mix over thirty days 54.2% press, 41.6% observed, 3.7% reports, 0.6% academic.

Nothing is built by this PR.
params.title: What we have: the inventory, measured, with the right word on each layer
